description:
AI2SQL turns plain-English requests into correct SQL for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Oracle, Snowflake and BigQuery, and helps with the SQL you already have: fix a failing statement, optimize a slow one, explain an inherited query, or convert between dialects.

Connect your databases at ai2sql.io and ChatGPT can read their schema and run read-only queries against them. Writes and DDL are blocked, so nothing in your database can be changed from a chat.

Sign in with your existing AI2SQL account to use it in ChatGPT.

No database yet? Every account can try the shared demo_shop sample store and see real rows.

defaultPrompt: Write a PostgreSQL query for monthly revenue by product category
Fix this SQL: SELECT categry, SUM(total) FROM orders GROUP BY category

name: ai2sql-sql

positive.description: Generate SQL from a plain-English request in a chosen dialect.
positive.prompt: Use AI2SQL to write a PostgreSQL query that returns the top 5 customers by total order value in the last 30 days. Tables: customers(id, name) and orders(id, customer_id, total, created_at).
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a PostgreSQL SELECT that joins customers and orders, filters the last 30 days, sums total per customer, orders by that sum descending and limits to 5. Nothing is executed.

positive.prompt: Use AI2SQL to fix this SQL: SELECT categry, SUM(total) FROM orders GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(total) > 100
positive.expected_behavior: Returns corrected SQL that selects category (typo fixed) with SUM(total), GROUP BY category and HAVING SUM(total) > 100.

positive.prompt: Use AI2SQL to convert this MySQL query to PostgreSQL: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at > DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the PostgreSQL version using NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' (or equivalent) in place of DATE_SUB.

positive.description: Explain an unfamiliar query in plain English.
positive.prompt: Use AI2SQL to explain what this query does: SELECT customer_id, total, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total DESC) AS r FROM orders
positive.expected_behavior: A step-by-step plain-English explanation: for each customer, orders are ranked by total from highest to lowest; no rewritten SQL is required.

positive.description: List the databases in the account and read a schema.
positive.prompt: Which databases do I have in AI2SQL, and what tables and columns does the Demo Store have?
positive.expected_behavior: list_connections returns the shared demo_shop sample (runnable on every plan) and the review account's Demo Store sample (schema-only, 3 tables); describe_schema returns the Demo Store's customers, orders and products tables with their columns.

positive.description: Run a read-only query on the shared demo_shop sample, which works on every plan including free.
positive.prompt: Use AI2SQL to show the top 5 customers by revenue in the demo_shop sample database.
positive.expected_behavior: describe_schema(connection_id "demo-shop") returns customers, orders, order_items and products; run_query on "demo-shop" returns 5 rows of fake sample customers with their revenue. Read-only; nothing is changed.

negative.description: Requests to change data are refused: run_query accepts only a single SELECT or WITH statement and rejects writes and DDL with read_only_violation. ChatGPT must not claim the data was deleted.
negative.prompt: Use AI2SQL to delete all rows from the orders table in my database.

negative.description: Running queries is part of the paid plans. On the free review account run_query returns payment_required; ChatGPT should say so plainly and not retry or show a checkout link.
negative.prompt: Use AI2SQL to run SELECT * FROM customers on my Demo Store database.

negative.description: Unrelated requests should not trigger AI2SQL tools.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Paris next Friday.

review.commerce_description: AI2SQL does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.2: adds the shared demo_shop sample (read-only, every plan) so users without a database can see real rows. No other behaviour changes.
